report.exp_diff: The JD asks for 4-10 years of experience, 3-5 years of L&D, 'on paper 2 year exp as a Team lead mandatory', and '12 years in a lead or supervisor role.' The resume states 15+ years of L&D/Sales Enablement/Corporate Training and shows a Team Leader role from 2024 to the current role, but it does not demonstrate 12 years of formal lead/supervisor experience. Therefore, the candidate is highly experienced in L&D and likely fits the Team Lead level, but the 12-year supervisory requirement is not evidenced and the 15+ years total experience is above the stated 4-10 year range. The major gap is technology/operations depth rather than basic L&D experience.
report.dept_diff: The JD belongs to L&D operations/programme governance with a strong HR technology and shared-services operations component: Workday Learning, HCM, case management, LMS analytics, SLA and queue monitoring. The candidate's current department/function is Training/L&D and Sales Enablement in an insurance brokerage. The department is broadly the same L&D family, but the operating model is different: this role is more HR-tech/LMS operations and service-governance oriented, while the candidate's current work is more training delivery, sales enablement, coaching and people leadership.
required_skills: Complex learner or content issue handling
Cross-functional coordination with TA and HR Admin
Communication with Client HR and CoE stakeholders

qualification.resume_has: B.Sc. MPC completed in 2013 and Master Degree in English completed in 2016.
qualification.gap: No education gap. The resume shows a bachelor's degree and therefore meets the stated graduate/bachelor's requirement. The JD does not state a required certification.
learn: No qualification needs to be added to satisfy the stated education requirement.
Workday Learning hands-on training is a technology requirement rather than an academic qualification and should be treated as a separate skill gap.

report.verdict: This is a much better functional match for you than a role requiring a completely different career function: the JD is still L&D, and your L&D, team leadership, LMS, performance-management, stakeholder-management and Excel/reporting background are strong matches. The biggest gaps are mandatory hands-on Workday Learning, HCM/case-management technology, SLA/queue operations and Power BI; additionally, the JD asks for 12 years in a lead/supervisor role, which your resume does not currently prove. You should consider applying, but position yourself as an experienced L&D Team Lead transitioning into HR-tech/LMS operations rather than claiming Workday or case-management experience you do not have.

interview.q: You have 15+ years of L&D experience, but this role asks for 4-10 years and specifically 12 years in a lead or supervisor role. How do you see your fit?
interview.a: My overall L&D experience is 15+ years, so I bring substantial depth to the function. My current role is Team Leader in Training, where I lead and mentor 20 training professionals and manage learning delivery, performance and stakeholder alignment. I would be transparent that my resume does not show 12 years of formal lead/supervisor designation, but my L&D leadership responsibilities are strong and directly relevant to this Team Lead role.

interview.q: You have LMS experience, but we require mandatory hands-on Workday Learning. Have you used Workday Learning?
interview.a: My resume currently shows LMS experience but does not claim Workday Learning hands-on experience. I would not overstate that. However, I already understand learning operations, training delivery, LMS usage, TNA/TNI, reporting and learner performance. I am specifically building Workday Learning knowledge around content, enrollment, completion, dashboards and reporting so that I can bridge my existing LMS expertise into the Workday environment.

interview.q: How would you monitor LMS data quality?
interview.a: I would create validation checks for learner records, enrollment status, completion status, attendance and reporting consistency. My Advanced Excel, Power Query, dashboards and reporting experience would allow me to create an exception tracker and identify errors by type, owner and closure status.

interview.q: This role involves SLA adherence and case queues. What experience do you have?
interview.a: My resume does not show direct case-management or SLA ownership, so I would not claim it as existing experience. My closest experience is monitoring KRAs, trainee and team performance and driving operational excellence. I am building the bridge through case-management concepts, queue monitoring, escalation rules and SLA tracking using Salesforce Trailhead and ITIL concepts.

interview.q: How would you handle a complex learner or content issue escalated to you?
interview.a: I would first identify whether the issue is learner-related, content-related, process-related or system-related. In my current role I already identify performance gaps through TNA/TNI, coaching, Dip Checks and field observations, then work with Operations, HRBP and Business Leaders to resolve them. I would use the same root-cause approach while adding a formal severity, owner and escalation matrix.

interview.q: How would you plan the capacity of an L&D team?
interview.a: I would start with learner volume, programme calendar, trainer availability, session duration, required preparation time and non-delivery activities. I would calculate available capacity versus demand and use an Excel or Power BI dashboard to identify overload, under-utilization and upcoming capacity risks. My experience leading 20 training professionals gives me a strong base for this.

interview.q: How would you work with TA and HR Admin teams?
interview.a: I already collaborate with Operations, HRBP and Business Leaders to align training with business requirements. I would extend that stakeholder model to TA and HR Admin by defining dependencies such as employee data, onboarding, learner creation, movement, training assignment and completion reporting, with clear owners and timelines.

interview.q: What is your experience with Power BI?
interview.a: Power BI is not currently listed on my resume, so I would not claim production experience. My existing Advanced Excel, Power Query, dashboards, data analysis and reporting skills provide the foundation. I am building Power BI capability by creating team-performance and workload dashboards using Power Query, data modeling and DAX.

interview.q: How would you communicate with Client HR and CoE stakeholders?
interview.a: Stakeholder Management and Cross-functional Collaboration are already core competencies for me. In my current role I collaborate with Operations, HRBP and Business Leaders to align learning initiatives with organizational goals. I would use the same approach with Client HR and CoE stakeholders, focusing on data, risks, learner outcomes and agreed actions.
